To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the filtered backprojection (FBA) reconstruction algorithm for tomographic image reconstruction is optimal for sufficiently smooth functions, that a modification (MFBA) of FBA is optimal for weaker smoothness assumptions, and that the phantom view method is optimal for angular under-sampling.

(a) FBA and MFBA are optimal for reconstructing sufficiently many times differentiable distributions, (b) MFBA is optimal for reconstructing more general distributions than FBA, (c) MFBA is a limit of the well-established phantom view method.
the FBA is optimal in the sense of convergence rate, and that the MFBA is even optimal under weaker assumptions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical foundations of tomographic reconstruction, which are of interest in their own right.
the convergence behavior of FBA in the context of 3D computerized tomographic reconstruction and provides a theoretical justification for the use of this method.
the question how to choose the reconstruction method in tomographic inversion in order to obtain a given convergence order in both variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FBA and MFBA, as well as their semi-discrete versions, are optimal for the reconstruction of smooth density distributions in 2D tomography.
FBA is the optimal reconstruction method for the 2D inverse problem of computerized tomography, provided the data are sufficiently smooth and the sampling conditions are fulfilled.
FBA and its modifications are optimal for sufficiently smooth densities and that the phantom view method converges in the angular variable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the optimality of the FBA in the sense that it is the best possible reconstruction algorithm in the class of all linear algorithms.

we have proved optimality of the standard FBA under smoothness assumptions that are weaker than those in previous work, and we have introduced a modified version that is optimal for a wider class of smooth functions and that can be seen as an angular limit of the phantom method.
the FBA is optimal for the semi-discretization in the angular variable, while MFBA is optimal for a fully discretization in both angular and lateral variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to prove optimality, it is not necessary to assume that the data are noise free.
FBA and MFBA are optimal algorithms in terms of the number of views and the number of voxels.
the FBA is not just the most popular algorithm in 2d tomography but also the optimal one in the sense that it achieves the fastest convergence rate among all linear reconstructions.
